categoryName: Dry fruits, nuts, seeds and healthy snacking

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Premium California Almonds 500g; Happilo 100% Natural Californian Almonds; Vedaka Popular Almonds; loose badam by weight
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Nov-Feb (cold), exam months Feb-Mar & Nov-Dec, and Diwali/Gurpurab gifting Oct-Nov. Dips May-Jun when the residential school empties.
skuLines.marginBand: 8-18% (thin — price is well known; loose repack can reach 25%)
skuLines.notes: The single highest-rotation line in the category; soaked-almond-every-morning is a daily ritual for staff families and hostel students. Prone to dry-fruit moth/beetle in a humid monsoon — FIFO, airtight bins, monthly inspection. Repacking loose into own pouches needs FSSAI licence + Legal Metrology declarations.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Australian Almonds 500g; Mamra Giri (Iranian); Gurbandi/Choti badam loose
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting season Oct-Nov and winter; new-mother / convalescence buying year-round
skuLines.notes: Slow mover — carry thin or on pre-book/indent only. Ties up working capital fast at ₹3,000+/kg; do not stock deep before monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Premium Cashew Nuts 1kg; Happilo Natural Popular Cashews 400g; loose kaju W320
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; sharp peak Oct-Nov (Diwali/Bandi Chhor, Gurpurab sweets) and Jan (Maghi/Lohri langar sweets)
skuLines.notes: Also a kitchen input for langar/canteen sweets and gravies, so the campus kitchens create bulk demand alongside household demand. Grade fraud is the classic trap — buy on tested count-per-100g, not on a seller's grade claim.

skuLines.examples: Kaju tukda / 2-piece / 4-piece splits, loose; Vedaka Cashew Pieces
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks with festival cooking Oct-Nov and Jan; steady from canteens
skuLines.notes: The value line that stops a wallet leaking to town: same taste in a gravy or kheer at 30-40% less. Most stores skip it and lose the price-sensitive non-teaching-staff household.

skuLines.line: Walnut kernels — akhrot giri (Kashmiri / California halves)
skuLines.examples: Happilo 100% Natural Kashmiri Walnut Kernels; Nutraj Walnut Kernels; loose giri
skuLines.seasonality: Big winter spike Nov-Feb; exam-season 'brain food' spike Feb-Mar and Nov-Dec
skuLines.notes: Highest rancidity risk in the whole category (very high PUFA) — buy small and often, keep in the coolest part of the store, prefer vacuum/nitrogen-flushed packs, never hold loose kernels through a monsoon. Rancid walnut is the fastest way to lose a customer permanently.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj California Walnut Inshell 1kg; Nutraj Jumbo Walnut Inshell; local HP/Kashmir in-shell loose
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb (fresh crop + winter); a Diwali/Gurpurab gifting and prasad item
skuLines.notes: Shell protects the kernel, so it survives hill transport and a monsoon far better than kernels — the smart way to hold walnut inventory. Children crack them as an activity snack; near-zero packaging cost.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Roasted Salted Pistachios 400g; Happilo Roasted & Salted Pistachios; loose namkeen pista
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct-Nov; steady snacking through the year
skuLines.notes: Goes soft in monsoon humidity once a pack is opened — sell in sealed 100-200g packs rather than from an open bin Jul-Sep.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Pistachio Kernels 100gm; slivered pista for kheer and mithai
skuLines.seasonality: Festival and sweet-making months Oct-Nov, Jan, Apr (Baisakhi)
skuLines.notes: Small-pack only; a 50g/100g pack is what a household actually needs for a kheer, and it protects you from holding ₹3,000/kg stock.

skuLines.examples: Chilgoza in-shell loose (Kinnaur); Wonderland Foods Pine Nuts; imported pine nut kernels
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Jan (Himachal harvest + winter + gifting)
skuLines.notes: A genuine local-pride line for an HP store and a strong gift item, but extreme price per kg — stock on pre-book/indent, in-shell only, and only for the Oct-Jan window.

skuLines.line: Exotic nuts — hazelnut, macadamia, pecan, Brazil nut
skuLines.examples: Nutraj Macadamia Nuts 100gm; Happilo Hazelnuts; Wonderland Foods Pecan / Brazil Nuts
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct-Nov; occasional baking demand from canteens
skuLines.notes: One facing each, smallest pack, no depth. These exist to make the shelf look complete and to stop a 'they don't have anything' verdict — not to turn stock.

skuLines.examples: Happilo Essentials Raw Peanut 1kg; loose Gujarat bold peanuts; Vedaka Raw Peanuts
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy Nov-Feb (winter roasting, Lohri/Maghi 13-14 Jan chikki and gur-moongphali); steady rest of year
skuLines.notes: The cheapest protein and the cheapest nut in the store — this is the line the low-income non-teaching-staff household actually buys weekly. High volume, low value, so it absorbs freight well on a hill route.

skuLines.examples: Haldiram's Salted Peanuts; Cornitos Roasted Peanuts; Bikano Masala Moongphali; loose bhuni moongphali
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; collapses May-Jun when the school is on vacation
skuLines.notes: ₹10-₹20 price points are what a school student's pocket money actually reaches. Keep the smallest packs at the counter, not on a shelf. Goes soggy fast once humidity gets in — small packs only in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Vedaka Raisins 500g; Nutraj Kishmish; Happilo Raisins; loose Nashik/Sangli kishmish
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks Oct-Nov and Jan for prasad/sweets
skuLines.notes: Cheap, universally used, and a prasad/panjiri staple — a must-carry even before almonds by household penetration. Sticky and sugar-bloomed in a wet monsoon; keep sealed and rotate.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Munakka Raisins 200gm; Wonderland Foods Black Raisins; loose munakka
skuLines.seasonality: Winter Nov-Feb; steady medicinal demand year-round
skuLines.notes: Bought as medicine, not as a snack — constipation, anaemia, cough remedy, soaked-in-water for children and elderly. Low price awareness so it holds a real margin. Two grades matter: cheap black raisin vs. true large seeded munakka; label them differently or you will be accused of overcharging.

skuLines.line: Dates — everyday soft (Arabian / Kimia / Safawi / Zahidi)
skuLines.examples: Nutraj Arabian Dates 500gm; Happilo Premium Super Soft Kimia Dates; Lion Dates; loose khajur
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes in winter and for fasting/Navratri (Mar-Apr, Sep-Oct); Ramzan spike for Muslim staff households
skuLines.notes: Best value-for-money iron and energy source in the store and an accepted 'healthy sweet' for children — a high-conviction must-have for a campus with 5,000 residents including babies and elderly. Ferments and attracts ants in monsoon; sealed boxes over loose Jul-Sep.

skuLines.examples: Wonderland Foods Medjool / Ajwa / Mabroom Dates; Nutraj Medjool
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct-Nov; Ramzan; wedding season
skuLines.notes: A pure gifting and 'treat myself' line. Shallow depth, one or two variants; Ajwa in particular is bought as a religious/health gift rather than eaten daily.

skuLines.examples: Loose chhuara (red/white); Wonderland Foods Dry Dates; kharek for prasad
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov-Feb (winter, given to children with milk) and Oct-Jan for prasad and langar; wedding/shagun season
skuLines.notes: Under-stocked by modern trade and over-demanded by a traditional community — chhuara-in-hot-milk is standard winter practice for children in a cold hill household. Also a religious/shagun item. Very prone to worm infestation; buy fresh season stock and inspect monthly.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Dried Figs 250gm; Happilo Premium Anjeer; loose Afghan anjeer
skuLines.seasonality: Winter Nov-Feb; year-round medicinal demand
skuLines.notes: Bought for digestion, anaemia and bone health — the elderly and new-mother line. Grade (size/count per kg) drives price more than brand; keep one honest mid grade rather than two confusing ones.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Turkish Apricots (Pitted) 200gm; Farmley Dried Apricots 200g; loose Ladakhi khumani
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; local Himalayan crop Jun-Aug; winter demand Nov-Feb
skuLines.notes: Carry both: the soft sulphured Turkish for eating and the hard sun-dried Himalayan khumani (with kernel) which the local and Ladakhi-origin households specifically ask for. The Indian one is cheaper, travels better, and is a regional-authenticity win.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Dried Prunes 200gm; Wonderland Foods Prunes; Sunsweet
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Almost entirely a constipation/digestion purchase for elderly residents and post-partum mothers. Steady, unglamorous, reliable — stock one grade, 200-250g.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Dried Cranberries (Sliced) 180g; Farmley Dried Cranberry 200g; Happilo Cranberries
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; baking demand Oct-Dec (cakes) from canteens and households
skuLines.notes: The gateway 'modern' dried fruit — goes into muesli, cakes, salads and trail mixes; young university residents recognise it. Excellent margin, long shelf life, low breakage. Sticky in humidity; sealed pouches only.

skuLines.line: Premium dried berries — blueberry, strawberry, cherry
skuLines.examples: Nutraj Dried Blueberries 150gm; Wonderland Foods Dried Blueberries; Farmley Berry Mix 200g
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct-Nov; year-round for muesli users
skuLines.notes: High margin, low volume, very long shelf life — a safe way to add premium visual depth to the shelf without spoilage risk on a hill route.

skuLines.line: Dried tropical slices — kiwi, pineapple, mango, papaya, amla candy
skuLines.examples: Nutraj Dried Kiwi Slices 200gm; Wonderland Foods Dried Pineapple; sweet/salted amla candy
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; school-term only (collapses May-Jun)
skuLines.notes: Children's 'sweet that is allowed' — sells hard to the 5-18 hostel cohort at small pack sizes. Amla candy in particular is a cheap, high-margin, locally-accepted impulse item. Mostly added sugar, so keep it honest and separate from the no-added-sugar shelf.

skuLines.line: Dry coconut — gola (whole copra) + khopra slices/chips
skuLines.examples: Loose whole gola; khopra dry slices; Wonderland Foods Desiccated Coconut
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Oct-Jan (prasad, langar, Lohri/Maghi) and around every religious observance; steady year-round
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable in a Sikh institutional setting — prasad, langar sweets, panjiri and shagun all use it, and it is the item residents will make a trip to town for if it is out of stock. Cheap, long shelf life, tolerant of hill transport. Watch for mould in monsoon.

skuLines.examples: Nourish You Black Chia Seeds 250g; Nutraj Chia Seeds 200gm; True Elements Chia
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Jan (new-year health resolutions) and summer (sabja/chia drinks)
skuLines.notes: Seeds are now a daily habit, not a specialty — and they carry the best margin in the category because price awareness is low. Long shelf life, light, cheap to freight. The easiest incremental profit line for ARY in this whole lane.

skuLines.examples: Nourish You Flax Seeds 250g; Nutraj Flax Seeds 200gm; roasted alsi loose
skuLines.seasonality: Winter Nov-Feb (alsi pinni/laddoo is a Punjabi winter staple); year-round health demand
skuLines.notes: Two demands, one seed: modern omega-3 health buyers and traditional alsi-pinni makers in winter. Ground flax goes rancid within days — sell whole seed and offer grinding on demand rather than stocking pre-ground powder.

skuLines.line: Pumpkin seeds — kaddu ke beej / magaz
skuLines.examples: Happilo Premium Pumpkin Seeds 200g; Nourish You Pumpkin Seeds 250g; Nutraj Pumpkin Seeds 500g jar
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: The most-bought single seed after chia; also a zinc/immunity claim that resonates with parents. Roasted-salted variant doubles as an impulse snack — carry both raw (for health) and roasted (for snacking).

skuLines.examples: Nourish You Sunflower Seeds 250g; Nutraj Sunflower Seeds 200gm; True Elements Sunflower
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round
skuLines.notes: Cheapest seed on the shelf — the entry point for a household trying seeds for the first time, and a good bulk filler for own-made trail mixes.

skuLines.examples: Nourish You Watermelon Seeds 100g; loose magaz
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Oct-Nov and Jan (mithai/sweets); Navratri fasting Mar-Apr and Sep-Oct
skuLines.notes: Traditional sweet-and-thandai ingredient that modern trade barely stocks — a real 'we have it, town has it' win. Small packs; rancidity risk is moderate.

skuLines.line: Char magaz — four-seed melon kernel mix
skuLines.examples: Loose char magaz; Wonderland Foods Char Magaz; kharbooja beej
skuLines.seasonality: Festival sweet-making Oct-Nov, Jan, Apr; summer thandai May-Jun
skuLines.notes: Nobody in the household can make proper kheer, thandai or panjiri without it, and it is exactly the item a hill store forgets. Low value per unit, high goodwill per unit.

skuLines.examples: Loose safed til / kala til; Tata Sampann Sesame; Nutraj Sesame Seeds
skuLines.seasonality: Enormous spike Dec-Jan for Lohri and Maghi (13-14 Jan) — til-gud, revdi, gajak, til laddoo; steady rest of year
skuLines.notes: Maghi is a major Sikh observance and Lohri is a Punjabi household fixture — plan a 4-6x til/gur build-up for the first half of January and land it before the December hill weather closes the road. Black til carries a separate religious/ritual demand.

skuLines.examples: Nourish You Sabja Seeds; loose tukmaria; True Elements Basil Seeds
skuLines.seasonality: Summer Apr-Jun (falooda, sherbet, cooling drinks) — but note the school empties May-Jun, so it is really an Apr and staff-family line
skuLines.notes: Very cheap to stock, very long shelf life, negligible risk. Sells as a 'body cooling' remedy as much as a food.

skuLines.examples: Nutraj Seeds Combo Pack 800g (4-pack) ₹469; Happilo Sweet & Crunchy Seeds & Berries Mix 200g; Wonderland Nuts & Seeds Mix 100g
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Jan health-resolution spike
skuLines.notes: Higher ticket than a single seed and removes the customer's decision — the single best value-per-shelf-inch play in the seeds block. ARY can also assemble its own mix from bulk singles at a much better margin than a branded combo.

skuLines.examples: Loose chironji; Wonderland Foods Chironji
skuLines.seasonality: Festival and sweet-making Oct-Nov, Jan, Apr; wedding season
skuLines.notes: Expensive per kg but bought in 25-50g quantities, so the ticket is small and the margin is excellent. Absolutely a must-carry for panjiri, kheer and halwa in a traditional North Indian community; goes rancid, so smallest packs and fast rotation.

skuLines.examples: Loose gond (babool/kikar); gond katira crystals; Organic gond 100g packs
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy Oct-Feb (gond laddoo / panjiri is the standard Punjabi winter and post-partum food); gond katira spikes Apr-Jun as a summer coolant
skuLines.notes: This is the line that matters most for MARRIED STAFF WITH BABIES — gond-laddoo/panjiri is what a new mother in this community is fed for weeks after delivery. If it is out of stock in November, a family makes a 30-50 km trip. Two distinct products, both cheap, both long shelf life: stock both.

skuLines.examples: Loose 4-suta/5-suta makhana; Farmley Plain Makhana; Wonderland Foods Makhana
skuLines.seasonality: Big spikes at Navratri/fasting (Mar-Apr, Sep-Oct) — makhana is the classic vrat food; steady year-round, winter kheer demand Nov-Feb
skuLines.notes: Fasting-friendly, kid-friendly, ghee-roastable at home, and Bihar supply has expanded sharply since the Makhana Board push — availability and price are both better than they were. Extremely hygroscopic: goes limp within hours of exposure in a monsoon hill climate, so airtight packs and silica, never an open bin Jul-Sep. Very light for its volume — freight is cheap but it eats shelf space.

skuLines.line: Makhana — roasted flavoured (peri-peri, cheese-chilli, chaat, jalapeno)
skuLines.examples: Wonderland Foods Makhana Chaat Masala / Cheese-Chilli / Peri Peri ₹199-349; Farmley Roasted Makhana; Too Yumm Makhana
skuLines.seasonality: School-term months; collapses May-Jun
skuLines.notes: The single most successful new healthy-snack format in Indian retail in the last two years and the best replacement for a potato-chip purchase on a campus. Push the 20-40g ₹25-₹50 pack for hostel students. Shelf life is short-ish (6-9 months) and it dies in humidity — small packs, fast rotation.

skuLines.line: Panchmeva / panjiri dry-fruit mix (prasad and langar)
skuLines.examples: Farmley Panchmeva Superfood 405g; Wonderland Premium Healthy Mix 200g; loose panchmeva (chironji, makhana, gola, kishmish, chhuara)
skuLines.seasonality: Every religious observance; heaviest Oct-Jan (Bandi Chhor Divas, Guru Nanak Gurpurab, Guru Gobind Singh Gurpurab, Maghi) and Apr (Baisakhi)
skuLines.notes: A Sikh institutional township runs a religious calendar, and prasad/langar ingredient demand is predictable and repeat. ARY can blend this in-house from bulk singles at a much better margin than buying a branded pouch — subject to FSSAI licence and Legal Metrology labelling on the own-brand pack.

skuLines.examples: Happilo Premium Kashmiri Saffron ₹234; Baby Brand Kesar; Lion Saffron; Kashmiri Mongra 1g
skuLines.seasonality: Gifting Oct-Nov; winter kesar-milk Nov-Feb; pregnancy/new-mother purchase year-round
skuLines.notes: Tiny footprint, high ticket, no spoilage — ideal for a hill store. Must be locked behind the counter (highest theft-value item per gram in the shop). Adulteration is rampant; buy only from a source you can hold accountable, because one bad tin destroys trust on a closed campus where everyone talks.

skuLines.line: Almond / dry-fruit powder and badam-milk mix
skuLines.examples: Badam Milk Mix (MTR / Nutralite style); homemade badam powder; Dry Fruit Powder for babies; Sattvic badam pak
skuLines.seasonality: Winter Nov-Feb; year-round for weaning babies
skuLines.notes: Directly aimed at the babies-and-toddlers cohort — dry-fruit powder stirred into porridge or milk is standard practice for 8-24 month olds here, and for elderly residents who cannot chew nuts. Ground nut powder goes rancid in 4-8 weeks; small packs, or better, grind fresh on demand in store.

skuLines.examples: Farmley Trail Mix 200g + Berry Mix 200g ₹634; Happilo Trail Mix; Wonderland Breakfast Mix 100g ₹199; Nutraj Mixed Dry Fruits
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; term-time driven
skuLines.notes: The convenience format the 18-25 university cohort actually reaches for, and the best vehicle for slow-moving premium berries. Carry a 35-50g single-serve at ₹60-₹80 for hostel students AND a 400g jar for staff families.

skuLines.line: Roasted & salted nut single-serve packs (25-60g impulse)
skuLines.examples: Cornitos Roasted Cashew/Almond 30g; Happilo Roasted & Salted Cashews; Nutraj Roasted Salted Cashew 150gm; Haldiram's Salted Kaju
skuLines.seasonality: Term-time; collapses May-Jun
skuLines.notes: The whole point of this line is the ₹20-₹50 price point at the till — it converts pocket money that would otherwise go to biscuits or a trip to town. Keep it at the counter, keep it sealed (roasted nuts turn soft and rancid fastest of all).

skuLines.line: Roasted chana (bhuna chana) + chana jor garam
skuLines.examples: Loose bhuna chana (chilka + peeled); Haldiram's Roasted Chana; Bikano Chana Jor Garam; Vedaka Roasted Gram
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; heaviest in winter
skuLines.notes: The cheapest high-protein snack in India and the workhorse of a hostel/staff-quarter shop — chana-and-gur, chana in chaat, chana as a gym snack for university students. Cheap, robust, tolerant of hill freight, near-zero spoilage. Do not treat it as a low-status line; it will out-sell almonds by units.

skuLines.line: Roasted soya nuts / soya sticks / soya chips
skuLines.examples: Nutrico Roasted Soya; Soyabean sticks loose; Too Yumm Multigrain Chips
skuLines.seasonality: Term-time; Jan fitness spike
skuLines.notes: Cheap protein for the gym-going university cohort, at a fraction of a protein bar's price. Long shelf life, light, low risk.

skuLines.line: Dry-fruit namkeen / mewa chivda / nut-and-seed mixtures
skuLines.examples: Farmley Peri Peri Snack Mix; Farmley Tropical Savoury Snack Mix 160g; Haldiram's Nut Cracker; Bikano Khatta Meetha with nuts
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; guest/festival season Oct-Jan
skuLines.notes: Bridges namkeen and dry fruit — what a staff household puts out for guests. Fried content means a shorter shelf life and real rancidity risk in a warm store; buy in small lots.

skuLines.examples: Loose moongphali chikki; til chikki; dry-fruit chikki; Lonavala-style chikki; Jagdish Farshan
skuLines.seasonality: Massive Nov-Feb peak (cold hills + Lohri/Maghi); low in summer and in the May-Jun vacation
skuLines.notes: The perfect product for this location: gur + nuts, cheap, warming, culturally native, no cold chain, and children buy it with pocket money. In a cold hill winter this outsells almost every packaged snack. Softens and gets sticky in monsoon — de-list or reduce Jul-Sep and rebuild for November.

skuLines.examples: Loose Muzaffarnagar/Morena gajak; til revdi; gur patti; Deep gajak
skuLines.seasonality: Strictly Nov-Feb, peaking at Lohri and Maghi (13-14 Jan)
skuLines.notes: A true seasonal-only line — build it in November, clear it by end February, do not carry it into spring. Very high cultural pull on a Punjabi-majority campus in a cold location; a store that runs out of gajak on Maghi will be remembered for it.

skuLines.line: Dates & nut laddoo / energy laddoo (no added sugar)
skuLines.examples: Farmley Date Bites (Apple Pie / Dark Choco Orange) from ₹345; homemade dry-fruit laddoo; Rite Bite Nutrition Bar laddoo
skuLines.seasonality: Winter Nov-Feb; exam season; year-round for lunchboxes
skuLines.notes: 'No added sugar' is now the leading claim in this sub-segment. Strong fit for a school campus where parents and wardens want a sweet they can approve of. If made on campus by a canteen, margin and freshness both improve — but shelf life drops to 2-4 weeks.

skuLines.line: Fruit-nut bars / date bars (no added sugar)
skuLines.examples: Farmley Date Bites; Yoga Bars Chocolate Chunk Nut Energy Bars (₹450/10); The Whole Truth Energy Bars (₹760/10 x 40g); Nourish Organics bars
skuLines.seasonality: Term-time; Jan fitness spike; exam months
skuLines.notes: Sell singles, not just boxes — a hostel student buys one bar, a staff family buys the box. Long shelf life and hill-freight-friendly. MRP-driven so margin is capped.

skuLines.examples: The Whole Truth Protein Bars (12-15g, 8x52g ₹836) and Pro (20g, 5x67g ₹784); Yoga Bars 10g Protein Wafer Bars (10-pack ₹399); RiteBite Max Protein
skuLines.seasonality: Jan-Mar (resolutions/gym), term-time
skuLines.notes: Protein-forward is the defining 2026 claim in Indian snacking, and a university campus is exactly where it lands. But it is a premium, MRP-capped, slow-turning line — carry 2-3 SKUs deep enough to not be embarrassing, not a whole wall.

skuLines.examples: Yoga Bars Fruits Nuts & Seeds Muesli 400g ₹275; The Whole Truth Nuts Fruits & Seeds Muesli 750g ₹544; Nourish You Super Muesli 400g ₹315; Kellogg's / Bagrry's
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; term-time driven
skuLines.notes: Bulky and heavy for its value — the worst freight economics in this lane on a hill route. Carry 3-4 SKUs (one no-added-sugar, one chocolate, one plain fruit-nut) and let the mass brands do the volume.

skuLines.line: Peanut butter / almond butter / nut spreads
skuLines.examples: The Whole Truth Creamy Unsweetened 325g ₹185 / 925g ₹482; Open Secret Peanut Butter; Pintola; Alpino; MyFitness
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; Jan fitness spike
skuLines.notes: Now a mainstream grocery staple, not a specialty — cheap protein per rupee, 12-18 month shelf life, glass or PET jars that survive hill transport, and it is exactly what a hostel student eats with bread. Stock unsweetened AND chocolate; the chocolate one sells to children, the unsweetened to the gym cohort. Glass jars break on a bad road — prefer PET where available.

skuLines.line: Baked millet / ragi / jowar / quinoa chips, sticks and puffs
skuLines.examples: Snackible Desi Masala Ragi Chips 57g ₹50; Snackible Chatpata Masala Jowar Chips 55g ₹50; Open Secret Ragi Chips 30g ₹40; Too Yumm Multigrain Chips
skuLines.seasonality: Term-time; collapses May-Jun
skuLines.notes: Millet savoury snacking is actively displacing potato chips in Indian modern trade, and it is the honest 'healthier crisp' a school warden will allow. Sell the 30-57g ₹20-₹50 packs; the big packs do not move to students. Crushes in transit — pack rigid on a hill route.

skuLines.examples: Act II RTE; 4700BC Popcorn; Cornitos Popcorn; loose bhuna murmura/popcorn
skuLines.seasonality: Term-time; spikes around campus events, film nights and festivals
skuLines.notes: Highest-volume 'guilt-free' snack per rupee and a natural event/bulk seller on a campus. Enormous volume for very little weight — cheap freight but it consumes shelf space; and it goes stale fast once humidity gets in.

skuLines.line: Nut & seed cookies / oat & ragi cookies
skuLines.examples: Open Secret nut cookies; Snackible Coffee Cookies 70g ₹85; Unibic Oatmeal & Almond; Sunfeast Farmlite
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; term-time driven
skuLines.notes: The compromise product parents actually buy — a biscuit they can call healthy. Very long shelf life, robust, ideal for a route where restocking can be blocked by a landslide.

skuLines.line: Tutti frutti / candied fruit / glace cherry (bakery and canteen use)
skuLines.examples: Loose tutti frutti; Bakersville candied peel; glace cherries
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Dec (cake and plum-cake baking), birthdays year-round
skuLines.notes: Trivial cost, long shelf life, and it is the item a household or canteen cannot improvise when baking a birthday cake for a hostel child. Bulk 1kg for the two canteens, 100g for households.

skuLines.line: Dry fruit gift boxes and hampers
skuLines.examples: Happilo gift boxes; Farmley combo packs (₹825-979); Wonderland Grandeur Premium Healthy Mix ₹599; Nutraj gift trays; own-assembled 4-compartment tray
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp peak Oct-Nov (Bandi Chhor Divas/Diwali, Gurpurab), Jan (Lohri/Maghi/New Year), Aug (Rakhi), and wedding season Nov-Feb and Apr-May
skuLines.notes: Gifting has shifted decisively from mithai to dry-fruit hampers, and a closed campus with 5,000 residents and a large staff body generates real internal gifting (staff-to-staff, department gifts, visiting parents, institutional gifts). ARY assembling its own trays from bulk beats buying branded boxes on margin — but the window is short, so buy to a firm forecast and do not carry hampers into December unsold.

trends2026: Makhana went fully mainstream: flavoured roasted makhana (peri-peri, cheese-chilli, chaat, jalapeno) is now a standard modern-trade and q-commerce line at ₹199-349 for 100-200g, with 20-40g impulse packs at ₹25-50. Bihar supply and branding expanded sharply after the government Makhana Board push, so availability and price are both better than two years ago.

'No added sugar' date-based snacking is the fastest-growing new format — date bites, date-and-nut bars and date laddoos (Farmley Date Bites from ₹345) — replacing both mithai and cereal bars as the approved sweet.

Protein-forward claims are now printed on everything: 10-15g bars, 20g 'Pro' bars (The Whole Truth), 26g protein oats (Yoga Bars), protein chakli and protein chips. A university/gym cohort buys on the grams-of-protein number, not the brand.

Seeds have moved from specialty to daily habit. Chia, flax, pumpkin, sunflower and watermelon now sit at mass price points (flax ₹89, sunflower ₹99) and the 4-in-1 seed combo jar (Nutraj 800g ₹469) is the standard upsell. These carry the highest margin in the whole category because price awareness is still low.

Millet, ragi, jowar and quinoa baked snacks are actively displacing potato chips — Snackible and Open Secret sell ragi/jowar chips at 30-57g for ₹24-50, the exact price point that works for a school hostel.

Small-pack / single-serve is where the growth is: brands now ship 20-43g packs deliberately at ₹20-50, which is the only price point pocket money reaches. Stores that only carry 200g+ packs miss the student cohort entirely.

Premiumisation through named origin rather than brand — Kashmiri walnut, Kashmiri saffron, Mamra and Australian almond, Medjool/Ajwa/Mabroom dates, Kinnaur chilgoza. The origin word, not the pack, justifies the price.

Nut butters crossed into everyday grocery: unsweetened peanut butter at ₹185 for 325g makes it cheaper protein per rupee than almost any packaged snack, and it is now bought as a staple rather than a fitness product.
Gifting shifted from mithai boxes to dry-fruit and nut hampers, with retailer-assembled trays taking share from branded gift boxes on margin.
adjacentServices: Weigh-and-pack loose repacking counter — buy bulk almond, cashew, raisin, chhuara, makhana, seeds and repack into own 250g/500g pouches. This is the biggest margin lever in the category (8-18% branded becomes 25-40% own-pack) and lets residents buy 100g when that is all they need. Requires FSSAI licence for the repacking activity plus Legal Metrology declarations on the pouch (name, net qty, MRP, FSSAI no., batch, best-before, packer).

Grinding and roasting on demand — badam powder for babies and elderly, freshly ground flax, roasted til/chana/makhana. Ground nut and seed powders go rancid in weeks, so grinding on demand is the only honest way to sell them and it is a service town shops do not offer.

Institutional bulk indent supply to the two canteens, the langar/hostel kitchens and the F&V counter — 5kg/10kg packs of cashew pieces, raisin, chhuara, gola, til, makhana on a monthly indent. Predictable volume that de-risks the bulk buying that makes the retail repacking economics work.

Festive and gifting hamper assembly with on-campus delivery — self-assembled 400g-1kg trays for Bandi Chhor Divas/Diwali, Guru Nanak and Guru Gobind Singh Gurpurabs, Lohri/Maghi, Rakhi and the wedding season, plus department/institutional gift orders.

A 'panjiri / gond kit' standing order for married staff households with a new baby — gond, chironji, char magaz, almond, gum, makhana pre-portioned. This is the highest-goodwill, most predictable repeat need on the campus and nobody else within 30-50 km serves it.

An exam-season 'brain box' for Eternal University and senior school students (walnut, almond, pumpkin seed, dates, a bar) timed to Feb-Mar and Nov-Dec board and semester exams, sold through wardens and parents.

Monthly soaked-almond / daily-nut subscription for staff families and hostel wardens — a fixed 500g or 1kg standing order billed monthly, which converts a discretionary purchase into predictable offtake and fixes the buying forecast on a road that can close.
Pre-book / indent counter for slow premium lines (Mamra almond, Medjool date, chilgoza, pista kernels, saffron) so ARY does not carry ₹3,000/kg stock through a monsoon.

On-campus winter production tie-up with a canteen for chikki, gajak, til-gud patti and dry-fruit laddoo in Nov-Feb, using ARY's own bulk peanut, til, gur and nut stock — highest-margin, most seasonal, most culturally wanted output of the year.

Attach-sell airtight storage jars and silica sachets alongside every loose dry-fruit sale — a genuinely useful accessory at 173101's humidity, and it protects the store from 'your almonds went bad' complaints that are really storage failures.
